limitations_and_non_claims: This is a provenance and evidence-integrity review, not legal advice. License and rights conclusions are limited to the declared U.S. jurisdiction and to the metadata quoted at review time.

No legal clearance or exhaustive rights audit is claimed. Commons and institutional metadata were spot-checked for every pinned asset, but third-party rights, privacy, publicity, trademark, or jurisdictional issues beyond the declared fields were not exhaustively analyzed.

No asset body was downloaded during this review. Remote byte identity was checked with HEAD Content-Length and ETag/MD5 against local bytes and local MD5; remote SHA-256 was not available from the metadata used.
No training admission or training authorization is made. training_admitted is false, no model was trained, and no model-quality evaluation was performed.
No perceptual or near-duplicate detection is claimed. Only exact byte-level SHA-256 dedup and source-identity uniqueness were checked.
No exhaustive semantic decontamination or benchmark-overlap analysis is claimed. The check is limited to the declared excluded source IDs and fragments against source_id, group_key, and asset_id.
Content consistency was assessed visually against the declared title/subject for all seven derivatives. This is not a semantic or exhaustive content audit.
All seven current Commons page revisions equal the pinned revisions at review time; no current-revision difference required recording. Future page or file changes could invalidate the pins.

The split assignment is deterministic and was frozen before acquisition, but the protocol note states that a National Archives collection was added because the initial six-candidate set had no development group. Nonempty split coverage is therefore design-conditioned, not a claim of random sampling.

The acquisition receipt is not independently authenticated; its request history is receipt-declared. The selected evidence is internally consistent and its asset hashes/geometry are independently reproducible.
